scenes.img: In a royal hall, King Uttanapada: black beard, gold crown, maroon robes sits on his throne with Queen Suruchi: proud queen in red silk with heavy jewels close at his side, while Queen Suniti: gentle queen in a simple white sari with a blue border stands alone far away near a pillar.
scenes.text: King Uttanapada had two queens. Suruchi, whom he loved more… and Suniti, whom he hardly saw.

scenes.img: King Uttanapada: black beard, gold crown, maroon robes on his throne holds a small prince on his lap, while Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet climbs up eagerly to sit on the king’s lap too.
scenes.text: One day, Suniti’s five-year-old son, Dhruva, saw his half-brother sitting on their father’s lap… and he climbed up to sit there too.

scenes.img: Queen Suruchi: proud queen in red silk with heavy jewels pulls Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet away from the throne by the arm, pointing at him coldly, while the boy looks hurt.
scenes.text: But Queen Suruchi pulled him away. You cannot sit there, she said. You were not born from me. If you want this place, go and pray to Vishnu.

scenes.img: King Uttanapada: black beard, gold crown, maroon robes on his throne looks away in silence, saying nothing, while Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet stands before him with tears on his face.

In a simple room, Queen Suniti: gentle queen in a simple white sari with a blue border kneels and holds Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet, who cries in her arms; she strokes his hair gently.
scenes.text: Dhruva ran to his mother, crying. Suniti held him, and did not say a bitter word. Go to the Lord, she said. Only he can give you a place no one can take away.

scenes.img: Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet, very small, walks alone out of a palace gate toward a vast dark forest, determined.
scenes.text: So the little boy walked out of the palace, alone… toward the forest.

scenes.img: On a forest path, Narada: sage with a white beard, saffron robe, a veena resting on his shoulder bends down kindly to talk to Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet, one hand raised as if to say go home.
scenes.text: On the way, the sage Narada met him. You are only a child, he said. The forest is hard. Go home.

scenes.img: Narada: sage with a white beard, saffron robe, a veena resting on his shoulder sits with Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet under a tree, teaching him, one finger raised; the boy listens with folded hands and shining eyes.
scenes.text: But Dhruva would not turn back. So Narada taught him a prayer: Om namo bhagavate Vasudevaya.

scenes.img: In the forest of Madhuvan by the Yamuna river, Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet sits cross-legged in meditation under a great tree, tiny, eyes closed.
scenes.text: In the forest of Madhuvan, by the Yamuna, Dhruva sat down to pray.

scenes.img: Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet meditates through the seasons: a single image showing rain, then falling leaves, then snow around him, while he stays still, thinner, eyes closed.
scenes.text: First he ate only fruits. Then only leaves. Then only water. Then… only air.

scenes.img: Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet stands on one foot with hands folded above his head in deep meditation; the earth around him tilts and the trees lean, and small gods in the clouds above look on in wonder.
scenes.text: He stood on one foot, so still… that it is said the whole earth tilted under him, and even the gods held their breath.

scenes.img: Vishnu: blue-skinned, clean-shaven, four arms holding a conch, a discus, a mace and a lotus, tall gold crown, yellow silk appears in the forest, standing before Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet, glowing softly, the trees bowing around them.
scenes.text: And Vishnu came. Not in a dream. Standing right before him… blue as the sky, with conch, discus, mace and lotus.

scenes.img: Vishnu: blue-skinned, clean-shaven, four arms holding a conch, a discus, a mace and a lotus, tall gold crown, yellow silk gently touches the cheek of Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet with his white conch; the boy, wide-eyed, begins to sing with joy.
scenes.text: Dhruva opened his eyes, and could not speak. So Vishnu touched his cheek with the conch… and the child’s heart poured out in song.

scenes.img: Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet kneels with folded hands at the feet of Vishnu: blue-skinned, clean-shaven, four arms holding a conch, a discus, a mace and a lotus, tall gold crown, yellow silk, smiling, tears of joy, as Vishnu rests a hand on his head.
scenes.text: Dhruva had come for a place on his father’s lap. Now he wanted nothing else. He had found a love… no one could push him away from.

scenes.img: At the palace gates, King Uttanapada: black beard, gold crown, maroon robes runs with open arms to embrace Dhruva: boy about five, dark hair tied in a small topknot, saffron dhoti, small tilak, bare feet, while Queen Suniti: gentle queen in a simple white sari with a blue border watches, overjoyed, and people cheer.
scenes.text: Vishnu sent him home with a blessing. And this time… his father ran to meet him at the gates.

scenes.img: Dhruva grown up into a kind young king with a gold crown and a gentle face, seated on a throne, listening to ordinary people.
scenes.text: Dhruva grew up to be a kind and just king.

scenes.img: A vast night sky full of stars turning in great circles around one bright, still star at the centre, the pole star; a small boat on a calm sea below finds its way by it.
scenes.text: And at the end, Vishnu gave him a place in the sky that never moves. The pole star. Dhruva tara. Every other star turns around him.
Travellers once found their way home by that one star. The boy who was pushed away… became the light everyone finds their way by.
Krishna says in the Gita… Whoever sees me everywhere, and sees everything in me… I am never lost to them. And they are never lost to me.
